name: Bald Eagle
habitat: Forests near large bodies of water
funFact: Bald eagles can rotate their heads 180 degrees to scan for prey.
description: The bald eagle is a bird of prey found in North America and a national symbol of the United States. It is a large raptor with a distinctive white head and tail contrasting with a dark brown body.

name: Golden Eagle
funFact: Golden eagles can reach speeds over 200 mph when diving on prey.
description: The golden eagle is one of the largest and most powerful raptors in North America and Eurasia. Named for the golden-brown plumage on its head and neck, it hunts primarily rabbits and hares.

name: Peregrine Falcon
funFact: The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal on Earth, reaching speeds over 240 mph in a hunting stoop.
description: The peregrine falcon is a widespread bird of prey known for its incredible speed during its hunting dive. It feeds primarily on medium-sized birds caught in flight.

name: Red-tailed Hawk
habitat: Open fields, woodlands, and desert edges
funFact: Red-tailed hawks are often dubbed over other raptors in movies because of their piercing scream.
description: The red-tailed hawk is the most common hawk in North America. It is recognizable by its brick-red tail and broad, rounded wings. It hunts rodents and rabbits from a perch or while soaring.

name: Barn Owl
habitat: Farmlands, open country, and forest edges
funFact: Barn owls can locate prey in total darkness using their incredible hearing alone.
description: The barn owl is a nocturnal raptor found on every continent except Antarctica. Known for its heart-shaped face and ghostly white plumage, it is an exceptionally efficient hunter of rodents.

name: Great Horned Owl
funFact: Great horned owls have a grip strength of about 300 psi, comparable to a large dogs bite.
description: The great horned owl is a powerful nocturnal predator with distinctive ear tufts and deep hooting calls. It is highly adaptable and preys on a wide range of animals.

name: Snowy Owl
funFact: Unlike most owls, snowy owls are diurnal and hunt during daylight hours.
description: The snowy owl is a large, white owl of the Arctic tundra. Unlike most owl species, it hunts during the day, feeding primarily on lemmings. Males become whiter as they age.

name: Northern Saw-whet Owl
funFact: The northern saw-whet owl is one of the smallest owls in North America, weighing less than a soda can.
description: The northern saw-whet owl is a tiny, nocturnal owl named for its sawing call. Despite its small size, it is a fierce predator of mice and small birds.

name: Barred Owl
funFact: Barred owls are known for their distinctive call that sounds like Who cooks for you.
description: The barred owl is a large, stocky owl native to eastern North America. It has dark eyes unlike most other owls and a distinctive hooting call.

name: Long-eared Owl
funFact: Long-eared owls have asymmetric ear openings that allow them to pinpoint prey in complete darkness.
description: The long-eared owl is a medium-sized nocturnal owl with striking orange eyes and very long ear tufts. It is a secretive bird that roosts in dense vegetation.

name: Great Gray Owl
funFact: The great gray owl is the tallest owl in North America, though much of its size is feathers.
description: The great gray owl is the tallest owl species in North America with a massive facial disc. Despite its imposing size, it is relatively light and feeds primarily on small rodents.

name: Burrowing Owl
funFact: Burrowing owls nest underground in burrows dug by prairie dogs or ground squirrels.
description: The burrowing owl is a small, long-legged owl that nests in underground burrows. Unlike most owls, it is active during the day and perches on fence posts to watch for prey.

name: Elf Owl
funFact: The elf owl is the smallest owl species in the world, weighing less than a ping pong ball.
description: The elf owl is the worlds smallest owl, found in the desert Southwest. It nests in holes in saguaro cacti and feeds on insects and small invertebrates.

name: Mallard
funFact: All domestic ducks are descendants of the wild mallard except for the muscovy duck.
description: The mallard is the most common and widespread duck in the Northern Hemisphere. Males have a distinctive iridescent green head, while females are mottled brown.

name: Wood Duck
funFact: Wood ducklings can jump from tree nests up to 50 feet high without injury.
description: The wood duck is one of the most colorful waterfowl in North America. Males display elaborate patterns of green, purple, and white. Unlike most ducks, it nests in tree cavities.

name: Northern Pintail
funFact: The northern pintails long tail makes it one of the most elegant ducks in flight.
description: The northern pintail is a graceful duck recognized by the males long, pointed tail feathers. It has a chocolate-brown head and white breast stripe.

name: Green-winged Teal
funFact: The green-winged teal is the smallest dabbling duck in North America.
description: The green-winged teal is a small, agile duck with a distinctive chestnut head and green eye patch. It feeds by dabbling at the water surface.

name: Canvasback
habitat: Deep freshwater lakes and coastal bays
funFact: The canvasback is the largest and fastest diving duck in North America.
description: The canvasback is a large diving duck with a distinctive sloping profile. Males have a white body and reddish-brown head.

name: Canada Goose
funFact: Canada geese mate for life and can live together for over 20 years.
description: The Canada goose is a large waterfowl native to North America, recognized by its black head and neck with white chinstrap. Highly adaptable, it is known for its V-formation flight.

name: Snow Goose
funFact: Snow goose flocks can number in the hundreds of thousands during migration.
description: The snow goose is a medium-sized goose with white plumage and black wingtips. It breeds in the Arctic and winters in southern marshes.

name: Greylag Goose
funFact: The greylag goose is the ancestor of most domestic goose breeds in Europe.
description: The greylag goose is a large waterfowl with grey-brown plumage and an orange bill. It is the ancestor of most domestic geese.

name: Mute Swan
funFact: Mute swans can be aggressive defenders of their nests, charging at intruders.
description: The mute swan is one of the largest flying birds, with pure white plumage and an orange bill with a black knob. It is known for its graceful S-shaped neck posture.

name: Trumpeter Swan
funFact: The trumpeter swan is the heaviest bird native to North America.
description: The trumpeter swan is the largest waterfowl in North America with a wingspan up to 8 feet. Named for its resonant, trumpet-like call, it has recovered from near extinction.

name: Tundra Swan
funFact: Tundra swans migrate up to 4,000 miles each way between Arctic breeding grounds and wintering areas.
description: The tundra swan is a large, white swan that breeds in the Arctic tundra. It has a distinctive yellow spot near the eye and forms large flocks during migration.

name: American Robin
funFact: American robins can eat 14 feet of earthworms in a single day.
description: The American robin is one of the most familiar songbirds in North America. Recognized by its rusty-red breast and melodic song, it is often seen hopping across lawns.

name: Northern Cardinal
funFact: Northern cardinal females also sing, which is rare among North American songbirds.
description: The northern cardinal is a vivid red songbird with a distinctive crest and black face. Males are brilliant red while females are warm brown with red accents.

name: Blue Jay
funFact: Blue jays can mimic the calls of red-shouldered hawks to trick other birds.
description: The blue jay is a striking songbird with blue, white, and black plumage and a prominent crest. It is intelligent and vocal, known for its loud calls and bold behavior.

name: American Crow
funFact: American crows can recognize individual human faces and hold grudges.
description: The American crow is a large, all-black bird known for its intelligence and adaptability. It uses tools, solves complex problems, and lives in large family groups.

name: Common Raven
funFact: Ravens can slide down snow-covered roofs for fun and perform aerial acrobatics.
description: The common raven is the largest songbird in North America. Extremely intelligent, it has been observed using tools, solving multi-step puzzles, and manipulating other animals.

name: House Sparrow
habitat: Urban areas, farms, and suburban neighborhoods
funFact: House sparrows were introduced to North America in 1851 and have since spread across the continent.
description: The house sparrow is one of the most widespread and familiar birds in the world. Originally from Eurasia, it thrives in close association with human habitation.

name: European Robin
funFact: The European robin is a symbol of Christmas in Britain and appears on many holiday cards.
description: The European robin is a small insectivorous bird with a distinctive orange-red breast. Familiar in gardens across Europe, it is known for its territorial behavior.

name: Eastern Bluebird
funFact: Eastern bluebirds can see ultraviolet light, which helps them find ripe berries.
description: The eastern bluebird is a small thrush with brilliant blue plumage on the back and a rusty-red throat and breast. A symbol of happiness, it was saved from decline by nest box programs.

name: Western Bluebird
funFact: Western bluebirds are one of the few songbirds that nest in old woodpecker holes.
description: The western bluebird is a small thrush with deep blue plumage and a rusty breast. It nests in cavities and feeds primarily on insects caught on the ground.

name: Baltimore Oriole
funFact: Baltimore orioles weave intricate hanging nests that can take up to two weeks to build.
description: The Baltimore oriole is a striking songbird with vivid orange and black plumage. They weave elaborate pendulous nests from plant fibers.

name: Scarlet Tanager
funFact: The male scarlet tanager turns olive-green in winter, looking like a completely different bird.
description: The scarlet tanager is a medium-sized songbird with brilliant red plumage and black wings during breeding season. It is a shy forest bird.

name: Yellow Warbler
habitat: Shrubby areas, wetlands, and forest edges
funFact: Yellow warblers are one of the first songbirds to arrive on their breeding grounds in spring.
description: The yellow warbler is a small, bright yellow songbird widespread across North America. Its cheerful song is one of the most recognizable spring sounds.

name: White-throated Sparrow
habitat: Forest edges, brushy areas, and suburban yards
funFact: White-throated sparrows come in two color morphs that pair almost exclusively with each other.
description: The white-throated sparrow is a common songbird with a distinctive white throat patch and yellow lores. It has two color morphs that differ in behavior.

name: Dark-eyed Junco
funFact: Dark-eyed juncos are called snowbirds because they appear in southern states during winter.
description: The dark-eyed junco is a small, slate-colored sparrow common across North America. It is one of the most abundant and widespread forest birds.

name: Ruby-throated Hummingbird
funFact: Ruby-throated hummingbirds beat their wings 53 times per second and can fly backwards.
description: The ruby-throated hummingbird is the only breeding hummingbird in eastern North America. Males have an iridescent ruby-red throat.

name: Annas Hummingbird
funFact: Male Annas hummingbirds perform dramatic diving displays that create an audible chirp.
description: Annas hummingbird is a small, green hummingbird native to western North America. Males have a brilliant rose-pink throat and crown.

name: Black-chinned Hummingbird
funFact: The black chin of this hummingbird flashes brilliant purple when the light hits it at the right angle.
description: The black-chinned hummingbird is a small, common hummingbird of the western United States with a velvet-black chin that shows iridescent purple.

name: Belted Kingfisher
habitat: Streams, rivers, lakes, and coastal waters
funFact: The belted kingfisher is one of the few bird species where females are more colorful than males.
description: The belted kingfisher is a stocky, blue-gray bird with a shaggy crest and large dagger-like bill. Females have an additional rusty band across the belly.

name: Great Blue Heron
funFact: Great blue herons can stand motionless for hours waiting for the perfect moment to strike prey.
description: The great blue heron is the largest heron in North America, with a wingspan up to 6.5 feet. It wades in shallow water to hunt fish.

name: Great Egret
funFact: The great egrets long plumes nearly drove it to extinction in the 19th century for use in womens hats.
description: The great egret is a large, all-white heron with a yellow bill and black legs. Its near-extinction for the millinery trade helped spark the conservation movement.

name: Snowy Egret
habitat: Marshes, tidal flats, and shallow waters
funFact: Snowy egrets use their bright yellow feet to stir up prey from muddy bottoms.
description: The snowy egret is a small, elegant white heron with black legs and vivid yellow feet. During breeding season, it develops long, flowing plumes.

name: Green Heron
funFact: Green herons are one of the few bird species that use tools, dropping bait on the water to attract fish.
description: The green heron is a small, stocky heron with dark greenish-gray plumage. It is a clever hunter that sometimes uses bait to lure fish.

name: Greater Flamingo
habitat: Shallow lagoons, salt flats, and mudflats
funFact: Flamingos get their pink color from carotenoid pigments in the shrimp and algae they eat.
description: The greater flamingo is the largest and most widespread flamingo species. Its pink plumage, long legs, and curved bill are unmistakable.

name: American Flamingo
habitat: Shallow salt lakes, lagoons, and mudflats
funFact: American flamingos are the most brightly colored of all flamingo species.
description: The American flamingo is a large, bright pink wading bird found in the Caribbean and Galapagos with the brightest plumage of all flamingos.

name: Sandhill Crane
funFact: Sandhill cranes perform elaborate dances that include jumping, bowing, and tossing sticks.
description: The sandhill crane is a tall, gray bird with a red crown and long legs. Known for its trumpeting call and spectacular mating dances.

name: Whooping Crane
funFact: Whooping cranes were once down to only 15 birds in the wild, making them one of the rarest birds in North America.
description: The whooping crane is the tallest bird in North America. Named for its loud whooping call, it was saved from extinction through intensive conservation.

name: Purple Gallinule
funFact: Purple gallinules can walk across lily pads thanks to their extremely long toes.
description: The purple gallinule is a brightly colored marsh bird with purple-blue plumage and a red and yellow bill. It walks gracefully on floating vegetation.
region: Southeastern United States to South America

name: American Coot
funFact: American coots can sink slowly into water to hide, submerging up to their necks.
description: The American coot is a dark, chicken-like waterbird with a white bill and frontal shield. Despite looking duck-like, it is related to rails.

name: Wild Turkey
funFact: Wild turkeys can fly at speeds up to 55 mph and run at 25 mph.
description: The wild turkey is a large, iridescent bird native to North America. Males display elaborate courtship rituals. It is the ancestor of the domesticated turkey.

name: Ring-necked Pheasant
funFact: Male ring-necked pheasants have such vivid plumage that they were once used as models for dragon illustrations.
description: The ring-necked pheasant is a colorful game bird originally from Asia, now established across North America and Europe. Males have brilliant copper and green plumage.
region: Asia, introduced to North America and Europe

name: Northern Bobwhite
funFact: The northern bobwhite is named for its distinctive two-note call that sounds like its name.
description: The northern bobwhite is a small, compact quail with a distinctive white throat and eyebrow stripe in males. Named for its clear bob-white call.

name: California Quail
habitat: Chaparral, oak woodlands, and suburban gardens
funFact: The California quails distinctive head plume curves forward like a question mark.
description: The California quail is a small, plump ground bird with a distinctive forward-curving black head plume. It is the state bird of California.

name: Common Ostrich
funFact: Ostriches have the largest eyes of any land animal, nearly 2 inches in diameter.
description: The common ostrich is the largest living bird, native to Africa. Unable to fly, it has powerful legs and can run at sustained speeds of 30 mph.

name: Emu
funFact: Male emus incubate the eggs and raise the chicks alone for up to 18 months.
description: The emu is the second-largest living bird, native to Australia. It is flightless with vestigial wings. The male emu performs all parental duties.

name: King Penguin
funFact: King penguin parents can go up to two weeks without eating while incubating their egg.
description: The king penguin is the second-largest penguin species, found on sub-Antarctic islands with striking orange and silver markings.

name: Emperor Penguin
funFact: Emperor penguins can dive to depths of over 1,800 feet and hold their breath for over 20 minutes.
description: The emperor penguin is the tallest and heaviest of all living penguins. It breeds during the Antarctic winter, with males incubating the egg for about 65 days.

name: Rockhopper Penguin
funFact: Rockhopper penguins bounce from rock to rock using both feet rather than waddling.
description: The rockhopper penguin is a small penguin known for its distinctive yellow and black crest feathers. It navigates steep, rocky terrain by hopping.

name: Little Blue Penguin
funFact: Little blue penguins are the smallest penguin species, standing only about 13 inches tall.
description: The little blue penguin, also known as the fairy penguin, is the smallest species of penguin. Found in New Zealand and southern Australia.

name: Gentoo Penguin
funFact: Gentoo penguins are the fastest underwater swimming birds, reaching speeds of 22 mph.
description: The gentoo penguin is recognizable by the white stripe across its head and its bright orange-red bill. It is the fastest underwater swimming bird.

name: African Penguin
funFact: African penguins are sometimes called jackass penguins because they bray like donkeys.
description: The African penguin, also known as the jackass penguin for its donkey-like bray, is the only penguin species that breeds in Africa. It is endangered.

name: Brown Kiwi
funFact: Kiwi eggs are enormous relative to body size, up to 20% of the females body weight.
description: The brown kiwi is a flightless bird native to New Zealand. It has hair-like feathers, no tail, and a long probing bill with nostrils at the tip.

name: Superb Lyrebird
funFact: The lyrebird can mimic virtually any sound, including chainsaws, camera shutters, and car alarms.
description: The superb lyrebird is famous for its extraordinary ability to mimic sounds. Males have an elaborate tail that forms a lyre shape during courtship.

name: Southern Cassowary
funFact: The southern cassowary is considered the worlds most dangerous bird due to its powerful kicks.
description: The southern cassowary is a large, flightless bird with a distinctive blue neck, red wattles, and a bony casque on its head.

name: Scarlet Macaw
funFact: Scarlet macaws can live over 75 years in captivity and mate for life.
description: The scarlet macaw is a large, colorful parrot with brilliant red, yellow, and blue plumage. Found in Central and South American rainforests.

name: Blue-and-yellow Macaw
habitat: Tropical forests and woodlands near water
funFact: Blue-and-yellow macaws can fly at speeds up to 35 mph and use their powerful beaks to crack hard nuts.
description: The blue-and-yellow macaw is a large parrot with vivid blue upperparts and golden-yellow underparts. It is highly social and can mimic human speech.

name: Hyacinth Macaw
funFact: The hyacinth macaw is the largest flying parrot in the world, with a wingspan over 4 feet.
description: The hyacinth macaw is the largest of all flying parrot species, with stunning cobalt-blue plumage and bright yellow eye rings.

name: African Grey Parrot
funFact: African grey parrots are considered the most intelligent bird species, with cognitive abilities rivaling those of young children.
description: The African grey parrot is renowned for its exceptional intelligence and ability to mimic human speech. It has grey plumage with a striking red tail.

name: Budgerigar
funFact: Budgerigars are the third most popular pet in the world after dogs and cats.
description: The budgerigar is a small, long-tailed parakeet native to Australia. In the wild, it is green and yellow with black markings.

name: Cockatiel
habitat: Arid and semi-arid regions with scattered trees
funFact: Cockatiels are one of the few parrot species that can whistle tunes accurately.
description: The cockatiel is a small parrot native to Australia, recognizable by its prominent crest and orange cheek patches.

name: Keel-billed Toucan
funFact: The toucans colorful bill is surprisingly lightweight, made mostly of keratin with a honeycomb structure.
description: The keel-billed toucan is a colorful bird with a massive, rainbow-colored bill. Found in Central and South American rainforests.

name: Toco Toucan
funFact: The toco toucans bill contains a network of blood vessels that help regulate body temperature.
description: The toco toucan is the largest toucan species, with a massive orange-yellow bill tipped in black. Found in South American forests.

name: Great Hornbill
funFact: Great hornbill pairs seal the female inside a tree cavity during nesting, leaving only a small slit for feeding.
description: The great hornbill is one of the largest hornbill species, distinguished by its massive yellow and black casque atop its bill.

name: Rhinoceros Hornbill
funFact: The rhinoceros hornbills upward-curved casque can grow up to 7 inches long.
description: The rhinoceros hornbill is a large hornbill with a dramatic upward-curving casque on its bill. Found in Southeast Asian rainforests.

name: Laughing Kookaburra
funFact: The laughing kookaburras call sounds exactly like echoing human laughter.
description: The laughing kookaburra is a large kingfisher native to Australia, famous for its distinctive call that sounds like loud, echoing human laughter.

name: Pied Kingfisher
funFact: The pied kingfisher is the only kingfisher species that can hover over water before diving.
description: The pied kingfisher is a black and white kingfisher found across Africa and Asia. It hovers over water before diving to catch fish.

name: Atlantic Puffin
funFact: Puffins can carry 10 or more fish in their beaks at once thanks to specialized tongue and bill structures.
description: The Atlantic puffin is a small seabird with a colorful triangular bill and distinctive black and white plumage. Known as the clown of the sea.

name: Tufted Puffin
funFact: Tufted puffins can dive to depths of over 200 feet to catch fish.
description: The tufted puffin is a small seabird with black plumage, white face patches, and distinctive golden head tufts during breeding season.

name: Wandering Albatross
funFact: The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan of any living bird, reaching over 11 feet.
description: The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan of any bird, up to 11.5 feet. It spends most of its life soaring over the Southern Ocean.

name: Black-browed Albatross
funFact: Black-browed albatrosses can sleep while flying over the ocean.
description: The black-browed albatross is a large seabird with dark upper wings and a white body. Named for the dark stripe through its eye.

name: Laysan Albatross
funFact: The oldest known wild bird in the world is a Laysan albatross named Wisdom, over 70 years old.
description: The Laysan albatross is a large seabird of the North Pacific. It breeds primarily on remote Pacific islands.

name: Brown Pelican
funFact: Brown pelicans can dive from heights of over 60 feet to catch fish, with air sacs cushioning the impact.
description: The brown pelican is a large waterbird with a massive bill and throat pouch. It is unique among pelicans for plunge-diving from the air.

name: American White Pelican
funFact: American white pelicans fish cooperatively, herding schools of fish into shallow water.
description: The American white pelican is one of the largest North American birds, with a wingspan up to 9 feet. It scoops fish while swimming.

name: Magnificent Frigatebird
funFact: Frigatebirds can stay airborne for weeks and sleep while flying over the ocean.
description: The magnificent frigatebird is a large seabird with long, angular wings and a deeply forked tail. Males inflate a bright red throat pouch.

name: Northern Gannet
funFact: Northern gannets plunge-dive from heights of 130 feet, hitting the water at 60 mph.
description: The northern gannet is the largest seabird in the North Atlantic. It nests in massive colonies on sea cliffs.

name: Blue-footed Booby
funFact: Male blue-footed boobies perform an elaborate dance, lifting their bright blue feet alternately to attract mates.
description: The blue-footed booby is a marine bird famous for its vivid blue feet. Found along the Pacific coast of the Americas.

name: Red-footed Booby
funFact: Red-footed boobies are the most abundant booby species and the only ones that regularly nest in trees.
description: The red-footed booby is the smallest booby species, with distinctive red feet. It comes in several color morphs.

name: Great Cormorant
funFact: Cormorants have less preen oil than other waterbirds, which helps them dive but requires wing-drying.
description: The great cormorant is a large, dark waterbird found across much of the world. It spreads its wings to dry after fishing.

name: Common Loon
funFact: Common loons have solid bones that make them less buoyant and better at diving than most birds.
description: The common loon is a large waterbird known for its haunting wail across northern lakes. Its solid bones help it dive deep.

name: Arctic Tern
habitat: Arctic tundra, coastal areas, and open ocean
funFact: Arctic terns migrate from Arctic to Antarctic and back each year, the longest migration of any animal, up to 44,000 miles.
description: The Arctic tern migrates farther than any other animal. It experiences more daylight than any other creature.

name: Caspian Tern
funFact: The Caspian tern is the largest tern species in the world.
description: The Caspian tern is the worlds largest tern, with a massive red bill and black cap. Found on every continent except Antarctica.

name: Black Skimmer
funFact: The black skimmers lower bill is longer than its upper, allowing it to skim fish from the water surface.
description: The black skimmer is a unique seabird with a distinctive uneven bill. It flies low over water, dragging its bill to catch fish.

name: Herring Gull
habitat: Coastal areas, lakes, and urban environments
funFact: Herring gulls can drink saltwater thanks to special glands above their eyes that filter out excess salt.
description: The herring gull is one of the most common gulls in the Northern Hemisphere, thriving in coastal and urban environments.

name: Laughing Gull
funFact: Laughing gulls are named for their call that sounds like high-pitched human laughter.
description: The laughing gull is a medium-sized gull with a distinctive black head in breeding season and a laughing call.

name: Killdeer
habitat: Open fields, meadows, and gravel areas
funFact: Killdeer perform a broken-wing act to lure predators away from their ground nests.
description: The killdeer is a large plover with distinctive black breast bands. It is famous for its broken-wing display.

name: American Woodcock
funFact: American woodcocks have eyes on the sides of their heads and can see 360 degrees.
description: The American woodcock is a plump shorebird with a long bill. It feeds on earthworms and performs an aerial sky-dance at dusk.

name: Red Knot
funFact: Red knots migrate up to 9,000 miles nonstop from the Arctic to the tip of South America.
description: The red knot is famous for one of the longest migrations in the animal kingdom. It turns rusty-red during breeding season.

name: American Avocet
habitat: Shallow salt lakes, marshes, and mudflats
funFact: American avocets sweep their upturned bills side to side through water to catch tiny invertebrates.
description: The American avocet is an elegant wader with a thin, upturned bill and long legs. During breeding season, its head and neck turn rusty-orange.

name: Black-necked Stilt
funFact: The black-necked stilt has the second-longest legs relative to body size of any bird, after the flamingo.
description: The black-necked stilt is a striking wader with black upperparts, white underparts, and extraordinarily long pink legs.

name: Willow Ptarmigan
funFact: Willow ptarmigan change color with the seasons, brown in summer and pure white in winter.
description: The willow ptarmigan is a game bird of the Arctic tundra that changes plumage with the seasons.

name: Spruce Grouse
funFact: Spruce grouse are so tame they are sometimes called fool hens because they rarely fly from danger.
description: The spruce grouse is a forest-dwelling game bird of the boreal region, known for its tameness.

name: Ruffed Grouse
funFact: Male ruffed grouse create a drumming sound by beating their wings rapidly to attract females.
description: The ruffed grouse is a popular game bird of eastern North American forests with a distinctive drumming display.

name: Chukar
funFact: Chukars prefer running uphill to flying when escaping danger.
description: The chukar is a rotund game bird native to Eurasia and introduced to North America with distinctive black and white barring.

name: Common Crane
funFact: Common cranes perform elaborate dances with jumping, bowing, and wing-flapping during courtship.
description: The common crane is a large, elegant wading bird with gray plumage and a red crown patch. Famous for its courtship dances.

name: Demoiselle Crane
funFact: Demoiselle cranes fly at altitudes over 26,000 feet during their Himalayan migration.
description: The demoiselle crane is the smallest crane species, elegant and graceful with a black neck and white ear tufts.

name: Bearded Vulture
funFact: Bearded vultures eat bones, dropping them from great heights to crack them into swallowable pieces.
description: The bearded vulture is the only bird species that feeds almost exclusively on bones.

name: Andean Condor
funFact: The Andean condor has the largest wingspan of any raptor, reaching over 10 feet.
description: The Andean condor is one of the worlds largest flying birds. It soars on thermal currents over the Andes mountains.

name: King Vulture
funFact: King vultures were believed by the Maya to carry messages between humans and gods.
description: The king vulture is a large, colorful vulture with a vividly colored head and a white body.

name: Turkey Vulture
funFact: Turkey vultures have the best sense of smell of any bird, able to detect carrion from miles away.
description: The turkey vulture is a large soaring bird with a red, featherless head resembling a wild turkey.

name: American Kestrel
habitat: Open areas, farmlands, and urban edges
funFact: American kestrels can see ultraviolet light, which helps them track the urine trails of rodents.
description: The American kestrel is the smallest and most common falcon in North America. Males have slate-blue wings.

name: Merlin
habitat: Open country, moorlands, and coastal areas
funFact: Merlins were once known as pigeon hawks due to their habit of hunting pigeons.
description: The merlin is a small, powerful falcon found across the Northern Hemisphere. It pursues small birds in direct flight.

name: Prairie Falcon
funFact: Prairie falcons can reach speeds over 45 mph in level flight and much faster in a stoop.
description: The prairie falcon is a large, sandy-brown falcon of the western North American open country.

name: Gyrfalcon
habitat: Arctic tundra, coastlines, and mountainous areas
funFact: The gyrfalcon is the largest falcon in the world and was once reserved as a bird of kings.
description: The gyrfalcon is the largest of all falcon species, found in Arctic regions. It was historically prized in falconry for royalty.

name: Osprey
habitat: Near large bodies of water worldwide
funFact: Ospreys have reversible outer toes that allow them to grasp fish with two toes in front and two behind.
description: The osprey is a large raptor found on every continent except Antarctica. It feeds almost exclusively on fish.

name: Northern Harrier
habitat: Open grasslands, marshes, and agricultural fields
funFact: Northern harriers have facial discs similar to owls that help them locate prey by sound.
description: The northern harrier is a slim raptor that hunts by flying low over open ground, using both sight and sound.

name: Coopers Hawk
funFact: Coopers hawks are agile enough to chase prey through dense forest at high speed.
description: The Coopers hawk is a medium-sized accipiter that specializes in capturing doves and songbirds in flight.

name: Sharp-shinned Hawk
funFact: The sharp-shinned hawk is the smallest hawk in North America, barely larger than a jay.
description: The sharp-shinned hawk is the smallest accipiter in North America. A rapid, agile flier that hunts small songbirds.

name: Swainsons Hawk
funFact: Swainsons hawks migrate in massive flocks of hundreds of thousands from North America to South America.
description: The Swainsons hawk is a medium-sized raptor that migrates in enormous flocks to the pampas of Argentina for the winter.

name: Rough-legged Hawk
habitat: Open tundra and prairies in winter
funFact: Rough-legged hawks have feathered legs all the way to their toes, adapted for Arctic cold.
description: The rough-legged hawk breeds in the Arctic tundra and winters in open prairies of North America.

name: Ferruginous Hawk
funFact: The ferruginous hawk is the largest North American hawk, with a wingspan over 5 feet.
description: The ferruginous hawk is the largest buteo hawk in North America with rust-colored upperparts.

name: White-tailed Kite
habitat: Open grasslands, marshes, and agricultural areas
funFact: White-tailed kites can hover in place for extended periods while scanning the ground for prey.
description: The white-tailed kite is a graceful raptor with white plumage, black shoulders, and a forked tail.
region: Western North America and Central America

name: Mississippi Kite
funFact: Mississippi kites eat enormous quantities of cicadas and other insects caught in mid-air.
description: The Mississippi kite is a small, elegant raptor with pearl-gray plumage that feeds primarily on insects caught in flight.

name: Red-winged Blackbird
funFact: Red-winged blackbirds are one of the most abundant birds in North America, with over 200 million individuals.
description: The red-winged blackbird is one of the most abundant and widespread birds in North America with bright red and yellow shoulder patches.

name: Brown-headed Cowbird
habitat: Open areas, edges, and agricultural lands
funFact: Brown-headed cowbirds are brood parasites that lay their eggs in other birds nests.
description: The brown-headed cowbird is a brood parasite that lays its eggs in the nests of other bird species.

name: Common Grackle
habitat: Open areas, parks, and suburban neighborhoods
funFact: Common grackles have iridescent feathers that shimmer purple, green, and bronze in the sunlight.
description: The common grackle is a large, lanky blackbird with iridescent plumage and bright yellow eyes.

name: Great-tailed Grackle
habitat: Urban areas, parks, and agricultural lands
funFact: Male great-tailed grackles have a wingspan of nearly 18 inches and their long tails make up half their total length.
description: The great-tailed grackle is a large, noisy blackbird with a very long, keel-shaped tail.

name: Yellow-headed Blackbird
funFact: Male yellow-headed blackbirds defend small nesting territories within marshes, sometimes with multiple females.
description: The yellow-headed blackbird is a striking songbird with a brilliant yellow-orange head contrasting with a black body.

name: Eastern Meadowlark
funFact: The eastern meadowlark looks almost identical to the western meadowlark but has a completely different song.
description: The eastern meadowlark is a bright yellow songbird with a distinctive V-shaped black breast band.

name: Western Meadowlark
funFact: The western meadowlark is the state bird of six different U.S. states, more than any other bird.
description: The western meadowlark is a bright yellow songbird with a black V-shaped breast band, the state bird of six states.

name: Orchard Oriole
habitat: Open woodlands, orchards, and stream edges
funFact: The orchard oriole is the smallest icterid in North America, smaller than even the house finch.
description: The orchard oriole is a small, chestnut and black songbird. Males have a chestnut body with a black head.

name: Bullocks Oriole
habitat: Open deciduous woodlands and suburban areas
funFact: Bullocks orioles weave elaborate hanging pouch nests that dangle from tree branches.
description: The Bullocks oriole is a bright orange and black songbird of western North America that weaves hanging basket nests.

name: Barn Swallow
habitat: Open farmlands and areas near water
funFact: Barn swallows migrate up to 6,000 miles between their breeding and wintering grounds.
description: The barn swallow is the most widespread swallow species in the world with a distinctive deeply forked tail.

name: Tree Swallow
habitat: Open areas near water and nest boxes
funFact: Tree swallows are one of the few North American songbirds that can digest berries, allowing them to migrate earlier in spring.
description: The tree swallow is a small, iridescent blue-green swallow with white underparts.

name: Cliff Swallow
habitat: Open areas near cliffs and buildings
funFact: Cliff swallows build gourd-shaped mud nests in colonies that can number in the hundreds.
description: The cliff swallow is a small swallow with a pale rump and squared-off tail that builds enclosed mud nests in colonies.

name: Purple Martin
habitat: Open areas near water and nest boxes
funFact: Purple martins are almost completely dependent on human-provided nest boxes in the eastern United States.
description: The purple martin is the largest North American swallow with iridescent purple-blue plumage in males.

name: Bank Swallow
habitat: Open areas near rivers, lakes, and coastlines
funFact: Bank swallows are the smallest swallow species in North America and nest in burrows dug into sandy banks.
description: The bank swallow is the smallest swallow in North America, nesting in burrows excavated in sandy banks near water.

name: Violet-green Swallow
habitat: Open areas near forests and nesting cavities
funFact: Violet-green swallows have white patches on their face that wrap around to the back of their head.
description: The violet-green swallow is a small, colorful swallow with iridescent green and violet upperparts.

name: Chimney Swift
habitat: Urban areas, towns, and open country
funFact: Chimney swifts can spend almost their entire lives in the air, even sleeping while flying.
description: The chimney swift is a cigar-shaped, dark gray bird that spends most of its life on the wing.

name: Common Nighthawk
habitat: Open areas, rooftops, and bare ground
funFact: Common nighthawks have tiny feathers around their mouth that form a wide funnel for catching insects in flight.
description: The common nighthawk is a nocturnal bird that feeds on flying insects caught during acrobatic aerial displays.

name: Eastern Whip-poor-will
habitat: Deciduous and mixed forests with open understory
funFact: Eastern whip-poor-wills can sing up to 400 times per hour, repeating their name-like call all night.
description: The eastern whip-poor-will is a nocturnal bird named for its distinctive three-part call.

name: Greater Roadrunner
funFact: Greater roadrunners can run at speeds up to 20 mph and can live without drinking water.
description: The greater roadrunner is a large, ground-dwelling cuckoo of the American deserts known for its X-shaped tail.

name: Yellow-billed Cuckoo
funFact: Yellow-billed cuckoos are sometimes called rain crows because they call more frequently before storms.
description: The yellow-billed cuckoo is a slim, long-tailed bird with a curved yellow bill that feeds on caterpillars.

name: Eurasian Hoopoe
funFact: The hoopoe has a spectacular fan-like crest that it raises when excited or alarmed.
description: The Eurasian hoopoe is a distinctive bird with cinnamon plumage, black and white wing bars, and a spectacular erectile crest.

name: Tawny Frogmouth
funFact: Tawny frogmouths are often mistaken for owls but are actually more closely related to nightjars.
description: The tawny frogmouth is a nocturnal bird of Australia with cryptic plumage that perfectly camouflages it against tree bark.

name: Common Potoo
funFact: Common potoos perch upright on branches during the day, looking exactly like a broken tree stump.
description: The common potoo is a nocturnal bird of Central and South American forests with an enormous mouth and cryptic plumage.

name: American Goldfinch
funFact: American goldfinches are one of the latest nesting birds, often not breeding until late July.
description: The American goldfinch is a small, bright yellow songbird with black wings and cap, one of the latest-nesting birds in North America.

name: Pine Grosbeak
habitat: Boreal forests and mountain conifer forests
funFact: Pine grosbeaks are one of the tamest boreal birds, often allowing close approach.
description: The pine grosbeak is a large, plump finch with rosy-pink plumage in males. Found in boreal forests across North America.

name: Evening Grosbeak
funFact: Evening grosbeaks are irruptive migrants, showing up in large numbers far south of their normal range in some years.
description: The evening grosbeak is a large, stocky finch with a massive conical bill and bright yellow body in males.

name: Cassins Finch
funFact: Cassins finches are the most recently described North American bird species, not recognized until 1861.
description: The Cassins finch is a medium-sized finch with rosy-red crown and pinkish wash on the breast, found in mountain forests.

name: Red Crossbill
funFact: Red crossbills have uniquely crossed mandibles specifically adapted for extracting seeds from conifer cones.
description: The red crossbill is a finch with a uniquely crossed bill adapted for extracting seeds from conifer cones.

name: Pine Siskin
funFact: Pine siskins can carry salmonella bacteria without getting sick, which can be transmitted to backyard birds at feeders.
description: The pine siskin is a small, streaky brown finch with yellow edging on its wings and tail, an irruptive species.

name: Common Redpoll
habitat: Boreal forests, tundra, and weedy fields
funFact: Common redpolls can survive temperatures of -60 degrees Fahrenheit by eating seeds and fluffing their feathers.
description: The common redpoll is a tiny, streaky finch with a distinctive red cap and pink breast, breeding in Arctic tundra.

name: Hoary Redpoll
funFact: The hoary redpoll is one of the hardiest songbirds, living further north than almost any other passerine.
description: The hoary redpoll is a tiny Arctic finch, paler and frostier-looking than the common redpoll.

name: House Finch
habitat: Urban areas, suburban neighborhoods, and desert edges
funFact: Male house finches get their red color from pigments in their diet of berries and fruits.
description: The house finch is a small songbird common in urban and suburban areas with red or orange plumage in males.

name: Purple Finch
funFact: Roger Tory Peterson described male purple finches as dipped in raspberry juice.
description: The purple finch is a medium-sized finch with rosy-red plumage in males and streaked brown in females.

name: Eastern Wood-Pewee
funFact: The eastern wood-pewees call is so distinctive that the species was named after its song.
description: The eastern wood-pewee is a small flycatcher with olive-gray plumage and a distinctive, plaintive whistle.

name: Great Crested Flycatcher
funFact: Great crested flycatchers always incorporate snakeskin into their nest material.
description: The great crested flycatcher is a large, yellow-bellied flycatcher with a distinctive crest. It always includes snakeskin in its nest.

name: Eastern Kingbird
funFact: Eastern kingbirds are named for their aggressive territorial behavior, attacking birds much larger than themselves.
description: The eastern kingbird is a bold flycatcher with dark gray upperparts and a distinctive white tip on its tail.

name: Eastern Phoebe
habitat: Woodlands near streams and suburban areas
funFact: The eastern phoebe was the first bird ever banded in North America, by Audubon in 1840.
description: The eastern phoebe is a small, brownish-gray flycatcher that bobs its tail frequently and often nests on human structures.

name: Willow Flycatcher
funFact: Willow flycatchers are virtually identical to several other Empidonax flycatchers and are best identified by their distinctive FITZ-bew song.
description: The willow flycatcher is a small, inconspicuous flycatcher best known for its distinctive fitz-bew song.

name: Scissor-tailed Flycatcher
funFact: The scissor-tailed flycatchers long tail feathers can be twice as long as its body.
description: The scissor-tailed flycatcher is a distinctive flycatcher with extremely long, forked tail feathers. It is the state bird of Oklahoma.

name: Vermilion Flycatcher
funFact: The vermilion flycatcher is one of the most brilliantly colored flycatchers in the Western Hemisphere.
description: The vermilion flycatcher is a small, vividly colored flycatcher with males displaying brilliant red plumage and a black mask.

name: Common Merganser
habitat: Lakes, rivers, and streams with clear water
funFact: Common mergansers have serrated bills that help them grip slippery fish while diving underwater.
description: The common merganser is a large diving duck with a reddish-brown crested head in females and a dark green head in males. It feeds primarily on fish.

name: Hooded Merganser
funFact: Hooded mergansers have the largest crest relative to body size of any duck, which they raise and lower at will.
description: The hooded merganser is a small, striking diving duck. Males have a bold black and white fan-shaped crest with a rusty flank patch.

name: Bufflehead
habitat: Small ponds, lakes, and coastal bays
funFact: Buffleheads are the smallest diving ducks in North America and often nest in old woodpecker holes.
description: The bufflehead is a small, compact diving duck. Males have a striking iridescent green and purple head with large white patches.

name: Common Goldeneye
funFact: Common goldeneye hens巢巢内产卵后，雌鸟会用自己腹部脱落的绒羽覆盖卵。
description: The common goldeneye is a medium-sized diving duck with a distinctive round head. Males have a dark green-black head with a white circular patch near the bill.

name: Ring-necked Duck
funFact: Despite its name, the ring-necked duck neck ring is rarely visible in the field.
description: The ring-necked duck is a medium-sized diving duck with a distinctive peaked head shape. Males have a black back, gray flanks, and a white breast with a subtle neck ring.

name: Gadwall
funFact: The gadwall is often called the plain duck, but males have an elegant pattern of fine vermiculation visible up close.
description: The gadwall is a dabbling duck with subtle but elegant plumage. Males are mostly gray with black rear ends, while females are mottled brown.

name: Blue-winged Teal
funFact: Blue-winged teal are among the earliest spring migrants and latest fall migrants in North America.
description: The blue-winged teal is a small dabbling duck. Males have a slate-blue head with a white crescent in front of the eye. It is one of the earliest migrating ducks.

name: Crested Caracara
funFact: Crested caracaras are members of the falcon family but behave more like vultures, often scavenging on carrion.
description: The crested caracara is a distinctive raptor with a black cap, white neck, and orange face. Despite being in the falcon family, it scavenges and forages on the ground.

name: Palm-nut Vulture
habitat: Palm forests and wooded areas near rivers
funFact: The palm-nut vulture is the only vulture species that feeds primarily on plant material, specifically palm fruits.
description: The palm-nut vulture is a unique raptor of West African palm forests that feeds mainly on the fruit of the oil palm.

name: Black Vulture
habitat: Open and semi-open areas near human habitation
funFact: Black vultures have excellent eyesight and also use their sense of smell to locate carrion.
description: The black vulture is a common New World vulture with black plumage and a bare, dark head. It soars in groups looking for carcasses.

name: Roseate Spoonbill
habitat: Mangrove sways, marshes, and shallow coastal waters
funFact: Roseate spoonbills sweep their spatulate bills side to side through shallow water to catch small fish and crustaceans.
description: The roseate spoonbill is a large, pink wading bird with a distinctive spatulate bill. It feeds by sweeping its bill through shallow water.

name: Wood Stork
funFact: Wood storks are the only stork species that breeds in North America and use tactile feeding to catch prey.
description: The wood stork is a large, white wading bird with a dark, featherless head and a long, curved bill. It is the only stork species breeding in the United States.

name: White Ibis
funFact: White ibises probe mud with their long, curved bills and can detect prey by touch alone.
description: The white ibis is a medium-sized wading bird with white plumage, black wing tips, and a distinctive long, curved pink bill.

name: Limpkin
habitat: Freshwater marshes and swamps with apple snails
funFact: Limpkins are specialized apple snail eaters, with bills specifically adapted to extract snails from their shells.
description: The limpkin is a large, brown wading bird with white spotting. It is specialized in feeding on apple snails and has a distinctive wailing call.

name: Rusty Blackbird
habitat: Boreal wetlands, marshes, and boggy areas
funFact: The rusty blackbird has declined by over 90% in the past 50 years, making it one of North Americas fastest declining birds.
description: The rusty blackbird is a medium-sized blackbird that breeds in boreal wetlands and winters in the southeastern United States. Males are glossy black with rust-colored edges on feathers in fall.
